statement: For the linear function $f$, $f(2x) = 2f(x) - 5$ for all values of $x$, and $f(4) = 11$. What is the value of $f(1)$?

choices.misconception: I treated $f$ as if it were proportional and ignored the $-5$, so I halved $11$ twice and got $\frac{11}{4} = 2.75$.
I used $x = 2$ correctly to get $f(2) = 8$, but in the next step I forgot the $-5$ and just halved $8$ to get $4$.
I used the rule in the wrong direction, taking $f(2) = 2f(4) - 5 = 17$ and then $f(1) = 2f(2) - 5 = 29$.

hints: The rule holds for every $x$, so you may choose convenient values of $x$.
Put $x = 2$ into the rule to connect $f(4)$ with $f(2)$, then put $x = 1$ into it to connect $f(2)$ with $f(1)$.

solutions.reliable: Write $f(x) = mx + b$. Then $f(2x) = 2mx + b$ and $2f(x) - 5 = 2mx + 2b - 5$. These are equal for all $x$, so $b = 2b - 5$ and $b = 5$. From $f(4) = 4m + 5 = 11$, $m = 1.5$, so $f(x) = 1.5x + 5$ and $f(1) = 6.5$. Check: $f(2x) = 3x + 5$ and $2f(x) - 5 = 3x + 10 - 5 = 3x + 5$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
